cvEn:
Liron Lin, daughter of Rachel and Arnon, was born on Tuesday, 6 February 1984, in Ramat Gan. She was the eldest daughter of the family, and sister to Tomer.

When Liron was two years old, the family moved from Ramat Gan to the Kfar Ganim neighborhood of Petah Tikva. Liron attended the municipal kindergartens and then the local elementary school.

At the end of second grade, the family moved to Even Yehuda, and Liron joined the third grade at the local "Bechar" elementary school. The move was not easy, and Liron missed her friends from Petah Tikva. However, after an adjustment period, she made new friends and built a new social circle. After finishing elementary school, she continued at the "HaDasim" high school in the town, where she stood out as a gifted, diligent and beloved student. She completed her studies with great distinction, and in the class yearbook it was written about her: "The main thing is that there is an angel like Liron."

That yearbook quote reflects Liron's personality well. She was a cheerful, smiling child who loved to laugh and to make those around her laugh. She had high emotional intelligence and a big, generous heart, and she was sensitive to the needs of others. Whenever she was approached, she knew how to listen, support and encourage, and she was always ready to reach out and help, without expecting anything in return. Her sensitivity also found expression in dozens of poems and prose pieces she wrote, all in her unique style, which combined humor and emotion.

Liron was marked by unusual emotional maturity and inner strength. She believed wholeheartedly in the values and goals she set for herself, and she pursued them with determination and consistency. She had a well-developed sense of justice, perseverance and dedication to her aims, and she did not easily give up on things that mattered to her.

Her greatest love was for animals. From childhood she raised animals such as rabbits, parrots, fish, birds, canaries, hamsters and silkworms. Most of all, she was attached to Boni, her little poodle. Her love for animals was an essential part of her worldview and values. Liron believed that every animal deserves fair treatment and basic rights, and she applied the principles she believed in to her everyday life; she therefore adopted a vegan diet and took care to use products that were not tested on animals.

Her commitment to the welfare of animals also found expression in volunteer work. From the age of fourteen she volunteered with the "SOS Animals" association, took abandoned animals into her home and cared for their rehabilitation, spent many hours finding adoptive homes for dogs and other animals, and organized large-scale fundraising campaigns for the association's work. At seventeen she joined the "Anonymous" organization for animals, and took part in activities to raise awareness of the suffering of animals and to fight against medical and cosmetic experiments on them.

On 22 August 2002, Liron enlisted in the IDF and served in the Manpower Corps. She successfully completed a course for NCOs in personnel administration (terms of service) and was assigned to the "Amirim" signal battalion. Liron worked and helped soldiers with all her energy and determination, with a deep understanding of the importance of the task and the challenges involved in her role.

After several months in the unit, Liron asked to be transferred to another role, and her request was granted. She was assigned as a clerk at the Computer and Information Systems Center (Mamram) base in Ramat Gan, and in this role too she earned great respect and made many friends.

Liron blossomed during her army service. She enjoyed every moment, was surrounded by many friends, and spent time with them going out and on trips. During her service she also met Yuval, and they became an inseparable couple. In her songs she described Yuval as a "prince in a pure striped shirt". He gave her love, support, security and immense joy. Her relationship with Yuval filled her with tremendous happiness, and soon she became a regular presence in his home and he in hers.

Liron's dream was to become a veterinarian. During her military service she took a course in biology at the Open University and completed it with distinction. At the same time she registered for a degree in life sciences at Tel Aviv University, which she was due to begin immediately after her discharge from the army.

Sergeant Liron Lin fell during her service on 11 Tammuz 5764 (29 June 2004), at the age of twenty. She was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Herzliya. She left behind her parents and a brother.

On her headstone the family engraved the inscription: "'The mind refuses to understand, and only the heart sends a tear to the eye...' Our love is with you forever."

Liron left behind dozens of poems and prose pieces. Here are a few of her poems:

"Life is like the sky / full or empty / close or distant / bright or gloomy / stormy or calm / blue or black // There is one difference between the two / the state of the sky can be foreseen / but as for life, one can only hope..." (written December 1998).

"Like a narcissus on the shore / like a tree in autumn / like a cyclamen beside a rock // Like a sun that warms / like a dripping faucet / like a blue, blazing sea // Just as the seasons change / and summer becomes winter, and the reverse / so too I grow, change and mature // And when I lie on the green grass / dividing sky from earth / I close my two eyes / and think how the wheel can be turned back / I want summer to return to winter, and winter to summer, and the reverse / I want the mistakes born in the past / not to change the future, and the reverse" (written December 1998).

"The yesterday of tomorrow / a day with no definition / in fact yesterday / yet at the same time already tomorrow / without a defined identity / or a real definition / it continues to be / a day such as this / yesterday too / and in fact tomorrow as well...
A sad story about such a day / that cannot even find a place in the universe" (written June 1999).

"He looks into her eyes / and then bows his head / searching for shelter // She, as a helper opposite him, / supports him / gives him her shoulder to ease his loss / and he cries over her // Her hair, mixed with his salty tears, / absorbs his pain / and eases his suffering / now they are one / his pain inside her / part of her heart // For him she is a firm rock on which he leans / but in fact he is no more than a leaf blown by the wind" (written December 2001).

Liron's family continues her legacy of saving animals. Among other things, they donated medical equipment to the SOS Animals clinic, and in Yehoshua Gardens in Tel Aviv they built a building that serves as a recovery house for sick and injured animals. At the association's adoption facility in Herzliya they created a memorial wall covered in plants and a waterfall. On the anniversary of her fall, an event for children was held in her memory at the Herzliya facility, an event with awards whose theme was developing young leadership and community involvement through animals.

Liron is commemorated in Even Yehuda, on the memorial monument to local residents who fell in Israel's wars, and at the Manpower Corps memorial in Mahane Dori (Tel HaShomer) in Ramat Gan.
